name: source_loss_leverage
ecological_statement: For species occupying few islands, losses of equal population number can have unequal subsequent occupancy consequences because occupied source islands differ in source-access leverage and spatial complementarity.

future_primary.required_system: independent temporal island occupancy system or genuinely independent response-sealed source-loss system
future_primary.exposure: loss of an occupied source island between t and t+1
future_primary.preloss_leverage: source leverage frozen from t occupancy and response-independent island geometry before t+1 occupancy access
future_primary.outcome: subsequent contraction in occupancy or loss of occurrence support at t+1
future_primary.primary_prediction: loss of a higher-leverage source produces greater subsequent contraction than loss of a lower-leverage source

source_leverage_definition.effective_source_number: inverse Simpson Hill number of normalized graph-pressure mass across target islands
source_leverage_definition.high_leverage_source: defined prospectively from the pre-loss source-pressure contribution; threshold or continuous contrast must be frozen before future response access
source_leverage_definition.graph_semantics: paths traverse the full island graph; occupied sources are endpoints and intermediate islands need not be occupied

secondary_predictions.effective_source_number_decrement: larger N_eff loss predicts larger subsequent occupancy contraction
secondary_predictions.graph_empty_creation: losses that newly remove graph-reachable source support from target islands predict stronger contraction
secondary_predictions.spatial_complementarity: systems with complementary sources are more robust to loss of low-leverage sources but more sensitive to loss of unique high-leverage sources

guardrails: do not use v1.122 source-leverage diagnostic as confirmatory evidence
do not choose leverage kernels, graph scales or high-leverage thresholds after future response access
do not infer rescue, extinction or recolonization without temporal demographic or occupancy evidence
do not call graph paths realized dispersal routes
do not select a future system because its known result is favourable
same-dataset mammal threshold mining is closed
